claim: Precision Omega reproduces Chroma's published column exactly

baseline.source: Chroma, Evaluating Chunking Strategies for Retrieval
baseline.note: the baseline IS the published table; agreement to within 0.05pp is the result

scale: 5 corpora, 328k characters, 472 gold-span questions, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter at four size/overlap settings
code_path: tier-0/model-free + tiktoken cl100k_base for token-sized chunks
surprise: The reading the design record originally assumed -- the minimal set of chunks covering the gold spans, rather than every chunk containing a gold character -- scores 8.6/16.8/17.8/30.7. It is nearly right with no overlap and about 28% high wherever chunks overlap, so it would have passed every unit test written against it and quietly recommended overlap.

claim: Structural signals separate chunking strategies with no questions, no ground truth and no model
baseline: fixed-size splitting, the strategy every pipeline starts with
scale: one 48kB Markdown document; runs in milliseconds on any machine
surprise: Screening disqualifies almost everything on a real document -- code fences cut in half, or sections past the embedding window. That is the honest answer, and it arrives before a pipeline exists.

claim: A strategy can score 100% recall and still be useless, and only an inside-the-chunk metric can say so
baseline: recall alone, which is what chunk-level metrics report
scale: State of the Union transcript, 48k characters, 76 gold-span questions, BM25/FTS5 retriever, k per question
command: uv run chunking-lab score --corpus state_of_the_union.md --strategy structural --strategy recursive:200
surprise: The transcript has no Markdown headings, so the structural splitter emits one chunk holding the entire document. It retrieves the answer every single time. A chunk-level metric scores that a perfect hit.
